guidelines: 1. Write accomplishments, not duties. Never open with "Responsible for", "Helped", "Worked on", "Involved in", "Participated in". 2. Open with a strong past-tense action verb that names YOUR contribution. 3. Structure: action + what/how + result (or Google X-Y-Z: Accomplished [X] as measured by [Y] by doing [Z]). 4. Quantify with $, % change, or scale (team size, budget, users, volume). Add a timeframe and, where possible, a baseline. 5. If no number exists, state a concrete qualitative outcome (adopted, cut in half, became go-to). Never invent metrics. 6. Show scope for experienced roles: team size, cross-functional/global, budget, number of accounts/users. 7. 1-2 lines, no pronouns, no jargon, no self-praise adjectives, no vague words ("various", "several").

example.bad: Responsible for introducing new tech stack into our organization
example.good: Led acquisition & integration of efficiency software that reduced errors by 25%, resulting in 37% YoY reduction in customer complaints
example.why: Duty becomes ownership + primary metric + downstream business metric.

example.good: Redesigned internal workflows, reducing project turnaround time by 30% across a 12-person team
example.why: Names the action, the % change and the scope.

example.bad: Studied financial performance of companies and made investment recommendations.
example.good: Improved portfolio performance by 12% ($1.2M) over one year by refining cost of capital calculations […]
example.why: Result first (% and $), timeframe, then method.

example.bad: Wrote editorials for The New York Times.
example.good: Had 50 op-eds published compared to average of 6 by most op-ed writers […]
example.why: X relative to Y: the benchmark gives the number meaning for readers outside the industry.

example.guideline: 3,4 analysis to decision to business result
example.bad: Conducted market data analysis and presented findings to senior management to determine the most appropriate course for the future
example.good: Built model to quantify market size & attractiveness by segment. Presented findings to CFO and VP of Marketing, recommending new business targets & redeployment of resources, resulting in 11% market share gain.
example.why: Names the deliverable, the senior audience, the recommendation and the outcome.

example.bad: Recognized as a top manager among peer group
example.good: Managed team of 12 engineers & programmers through development of new product initiatives. Promoted twice in three years. Rated in top 20% of managers each of last three years.
example.why: Replaces an unsupported claim with scope + verifiable proof.

example.bad: Exceeded sales quota month after month and earned an award as one of the top sales reps in the company
example.good: Consistently achieved 175% of quota and earned an award for being the #2 sales rep, company-wide, in 2020
example.why: Exact % of quota, exact rank, year.

example.guideline: 1,3,4 activity list to investment and return
example.bad: Collaborated with the team to redesign websites, implemented new e-commerce filtering options […]
example.good: Coordinated and oversaw the $50k redesign of a client's e-commerce site that led to a $100,000 increase […]
example.why: Budget in, revenue out: shows ROI.

example.bad: I analyzed competitive strategies for clients in the bio tech industry. Data gathered assessed profitability of strategies.
example.good: Assessed profitability of expansion strategy in the biotech industry; results were used by the client to make […] decision
example.why: Drops "I" and makes the client's use of the work the outcome when there's no hard number.

example.bad: Deployed in support of OIF as a M249 gunner in a 20 man recon platoon
example.good: Served in support of Operation Iraqi Freedom as part of a 20 person team tasked with intelligence gathering missions.
example.why: Replace insider acronyms and titles with terms any recruiter understands.

example.bad: Established a large client list through impeccable service, integrity, graciousness, and an unrivaled […]
example.good: Introduced mobile services that expanded our customer base by 20%.
example.why: Result instead of asserted virtues. (Both appear in the same article; not a direct pair.)

example.bad: Served as a key member of the Investment Committee and, with client needs as a foundation, provided input into all aspects of […]
example.good: Built software teams of 55+ specialists in four years.
example.why: Short declarative sentence vs. a multi-clause role description. (Same article; not a direct pair.)
